the cell-free DNAs in the growth medium originate from micronuclei, and these micronuclei are derived from lagging chromosomes and/or anaphase bridges that form as a consequence of chromosomal instability.

the cell-free DNAs present in the growth media of cultured 143 B cells are composed mainly of repetitive DNA that originates from specific chromosomes and that these cell-free DNAs are derived from micronuclei.
cell-free DNA is a product of micronuclei and that micronuclei are a product of centromeric and/or pericentromere hypomethylation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the cell-free DNA derived directly from cultured human cells, and its origin.
the composition and origin cell-free DNA present within the growth medium of a human osteosarcoma cell line.
the identification of a novel cell-free DNA population that originates from secondary nuclear structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the majority of the cell-free DNA that is present in the growth media of cultured 143 B cells is derived from micronuclei that are formed from lagging chromosomes and/or anaphase bridges.
cell-free DNA is a mixture of DNA from apoptotic cells, DNA from necrotic cells, DNA from micronuclei, and DNA from other sources.
the majority of this cell-free population is derived from micronuclei, and that this micronuclei population is derived from cells that are undergoing a form of chromosomal instability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cell-free DNA is a product of chromosomal instability and that it is a reflection of the nuclear abnormalities that are present in the cell.
cell-free DNA in cancer is not just a byproduct of apoptosis and necrosis.
cell-free DNA is not a random collection of DNA fragments, but rather a collection of DNA fragments that are derived from specific chromosomal regions and specific chromosomal structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a significant portion of cell-free DNA originates from micronuclei, and the presence of cell-free DNA fragments derived from micronuclei can be used to assess the presence of genomic instability in a cell population.
the composition of cell-free DNA can be highly specific to the type of cell from which it originates, and this can be exploited to develop a novel class of biomarkers.
the composition of the cell-free DNA is not random and that it can provide a window into the chromosomal instability that characterizes cancer.
